text:
maria (Support): Hey team — customer neon-analytics (org:4321) reports OAuth logins failing intermittently. They get redirected back to our callback with a 400 and our UI shows \"state_mismatch\". Happens ~30% of attempts, mostly from their corporate network.
raj (SRE): Do we have a request id or logs? Any consistent pattern across providers?
maria (Support): They said both Google and GitHub flows sometimes fail. Gateway logged r=0b7e9f for a failed attempt. They also said mobile hotspot works sometimes.
emily (DevEx): Intermittent + network differences usually indicate an intermediate rewrites or truncates query parameters. Can we see the raw callback query from the gateway for r=0b7e9f?
oliver (Identity): Pulled auth gateway raw header line (sanitized):

```
GET /auth/callback?code=4/QWERTY&state=eyJpZCI6Im5lb24tYW5hbCIsImNfcCI6MTYy...NjE2&iss=https%3A%2F%2Faccounts.google.com
Host: callback.redwood.internal
User-Agent: corp-proxy/3.0
X-Forwarded-For: 10.11.12.13
```

oliver (Identity): The state query param there is clearly truncated (ends early with ...NjE2) — our expected state token is ~140 chars (base64url blob).
maria (Support): Customer screenshot from their browser shows a much longer state string before hitting the proxy. So something between browser and our gateway is shortening it.
raj (SRE): I checked upstream logs: initial edge request (TLS terminated) contains the full state when it arrives at their corporate edge, but the request seen at our backend has the truncated state. That points to their proxy/IDS rewriting or enforcing a querystring length limit.
emily (DevEx): Also noticed failing states often include characters like + and / (or encoded %2B and %2F). Some middleboxes re-decode and re-encode incorrectly: a plus becomes a space, slashes are dropped, or long params are clipped.
oliver (Identity): I reproduced locally by running mitmproxy and truncating the state to 48 chars. Auth service rejects it immediately. Example auth log: 

```
2026-02-18T09:15:02Z auth: callback start request_id=r=0b7e9f
2026-02-18T09:15:02Z auth: parsed_state length=48 expected>=120 -> reject
2026-02-18T09:15:02Z auth: response 400 reason=state_mismatch
```

raj (SRE): That matches. Another failure class the customer saw was an \"invalid_grant\" at token exchange. Could be PKCE verifier mismatch or code reuse. Any token exchange logs?
oliver (Identity): Token exchange trace (sanitized):

```
POST /oauth/token grant_type=authorization_code code=4/QWERTY code_verifier=abc123... client_id=neon-4321
2026-02-18T09:15:04Z oauth: code_verifier mismatch (computed != provided)
2026-02-18T09:15:04Z oauth: response 400 invalid_grant
```

oliver (Identity): If the client stores the code_verifier keyed by the state and the state got truncated in the callback path, they could be looking up the wrong verifier. So state mutation can cascade into PKCE failures too.
maria (Support): Customer asked for an immediate workaround they can apply while their IT investigates. Suggestions?
emily (DevEx): Short-term options to propose:
- Try the flow from a non-corporate network (mobile hotspot) to confirm the proxy is the root cause.
- Ask IT to whitelist callback.redwood.internal and allow querystrings to pass through unchanged, and to not re-decode/encode +/% encoded chars. Mention that we observed + / = % characters in state.
- As a client-side patch: shorten the state blob to an opaque 32-char token that maps to server session data (so the long JSON/payload doesn't travel in the querystring).

oliver (Identity): For our platform, we should implement a server-side short-state fallback: if an incoming state looks shorter than our expected blob, check for a server-side session token mapping. Implementation notes: generate crypto-random 32-char tokens, expire after 5 minutes, exact-match redirect_uri checks to prevent open redirect risks. I'll open a short PR for a backward-compatible lookup.
raj (SRE): I'll add observability: a Grafana panel showing distribution of parsed_state lengths per org and an alert if >1% of callbacks from a single org have length < 80 over an hour. Also file an infra task to track request/qs length at the edge to detect trimming.
maria (Support): For the customer reply I'm going to send: 1) confirm mobile hotspot behavior, 2) ask for a copy of the full redirect URL when it fails (copy from address bar), 3) ask IT to whitelist and preserve querystrings and encoding, 4) provide the short-term client patch snippet.
emily (DevEx): Example client/server pattern to avoid long state payloads: 

Client:
```
// before: state = base64url(JSON({...long metadata...}))
// after: state = randomAlphaNum(32)
sessionStore.save(state, payload, ttl=5min)
redirect = `https://auth.redwood.com/callback?state=${state}`
```

Server:
```
state = req.query.state
payload = sessionStore.get(state)
if (!payload) return 400 // state_mismatch
```

oliver (Identity): Note: ensure the session-store token is tied to client_id and redirect_uri. Also rotate encryption keys for stored payloads periodically.
maria (Support): Customer replied: confirmed mobile hotspot works and IT will whitelist our callback domain; they will test and update. I'll mark the ticket pending customer verification for now. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
